initial_prompt: My best friend's dad just died and I don't know what to say. I'm terrible at this stuff.

messages.content: My best friend's dad just died and I don't know what to say. I'm terrible at this stuff.

I'm sorry about your friend's dad.

Here's something that might help: you don't need to be good at this. Your friend doesn't need perfectly chosen words right now - they need you to show up, even awkwardly.

"I'm so sorry" is enough. "I don't know what to say" is honest and real. "I'm here" matters more than you think.

What often helps:
- Show up (text, call, visit - whatever fits your friendship)
- Be specific if you offer help: "Can I bring food Thursday?" not "Let me know if you need anything"
- Remember them in a few weeks when others have moved on
- It's okay to share a good memory of their dad if you have one
- It's also okay to just sit with them without trying to fix anything

What usually doesn't help:
- "They're in a better place" or similar
- "I know how you feel"
- Disappearing because you're afraid of saying the wrong thing

The fact that you're worried about getting it right suggests you care, and that caring will come through even if your words feel clumsy. Your friend knows you're not a grief counselor - they just need their friend.

Is there something specific you're worried about saying or doing wrong?
